blogs.title: The Pulmonary Mask: When the Chest is a Red Herring
blogs.description: An analysis of diagnostic anchor bias in the setting of recurrent pleural effusions. This post discusses how abdominal pathology—specifically Pancreatopleural Fistula (PPF)—can present exclusively as respiratory distress, leading clinicians down a misleading path of pulmonary workups and empirical treatments for tuberculosis or malignancy.

blogs.title: Beyond the ADA: Navigating High Amylase Pleural Effusions
blogs.description: A deep dive into the biochemical analysis of pleural fluid. This post focuses on the significance of pleural fluid amylase and lipase levels, the critical distinction between salivary and pancreatic amylase, and a differential diagnosis framework for amylase-rich effusions, including Boerhaave’s syndrome and malignancy.

blogs.title: From Pancreas to Pleura: The Anatomy of a Fistula
blogs.description: A look at the anatomical 'paths of least resistance' that allow pancreatic secretions to enter the thoracic cavity. This post explores the role of the esophageal and aortic hiatuses in the development of PPF following blunt abdominal trauma and compares the sensitivity of CT versus MRCP in visualizing these rare fistulous tracts.

blogs.title: Closing the Leak: Managing the Pancreatopleural Fistula
blogs.description: A review of the management ladder for PPF, from conservative medical therapy to surgical intervention. This post discusses the physiological rationale for using Octreotide, total parenteral nutrition (TPN), and bowel rest to suppress exocrine function and allow for the spontaneous closure of the fistula.

blogs.title: The Hidden History: Pediatric Trauma and the Art of the Interview
blogs.description: A discussion on the challenges of history-taking in pediatric populations, highlighting how social factors (such as bullying) can lead patients to conceal critical trauma. This post emphasizes the importance of iterative history-taking and the danger of premature diagnostic closure in the PICU/ED setting.
